plans.title: 2024 Gunnison Valley Housing Needs Assessment and SB24-174 Compliance Addendum (Western Spaces, LLC)
plans.body: Sponsored by GVRHA with Gunnison County, Crested Butte, Mt. Crested Butte, City of Gunnison and VHF; submitted to DOLA; DOLA required an amendment (memo Feb 18, 2025)
plans.finding: City of Gunnison needs 635-755 of the valley's 1,300-1,550 units by 2029; valley rental gap is 702 below-market units, with 418 rentals needed at or below 50% AMI.
plans.source_quote: 84% of the housing needed in the South Valley gets allocated to the City of Gunnison.

plans.title: 2024 HNA addendum - rental mismatch
plans.finding: 56% of renter households earn 60% AMI or less but only 8% of listings fall in that band; vacancy under 1% (Mar 2024).
plans.source_quote: while 56% of renter households make 60% AMI or below, only 8% of available rentals fall into this income band.

plans.title: 2024 HNA addendum - infrastructure constraint
plans.finding: City water margin tight (0.5M gal/day); Gunnison Rising lift station at capacity; development may need phasing with utility upgrades.
plans.source_quote: City of Gunnison Sewer: The Gunnison Rising lift station is at capacity and cannot accommodate additional flows without major upgrades.

plans.title: Gunnison Area Plan 2025 (with Special Area Regulations)
plans.body: Adopted by Gunnison County BOCC Nov 18, 2025, with an IGA with the City of Gunnison; city council adoption vote not confirmed
plans.finding: Sets the city Urban Growth Boundary (annexation-eligible) and minimum densities; draft SARs required 20% deed-restricted for 11-20 unit projects and 30% for 21+ du/acre in Urban Transition Areas (final text not verified).
plans.source_quote: The Gunnison Area Plan was adopted by the Board of County Commissioners on November 18, 2025.

plans.title: Gunnison County Strategic Plan (June 18, 2024 iteration)
plans.finding: County target: 300 new essential housing units by Dec 31, 2030.
plans.source_quote: the County will facilitate the construction of 300 new essential housing units of the 1,080-1,345 units identified as needed

plans.title: Prop 123 commitment filing - City of Gunnison
plans.finding: 68 affordable units by end of 2026; failure only means losing Prop 123 access in 2027. Progress toward 68 not found.
plans.source_quote: the city will lose access to Prop. 123 funding in 2027.

plans.title: Gunnison Valley Housing Needs Assessment (Rees Consulting) and 2021 Market Update
plans.finding: 960 units needed by 2026 (2021 update); city goal of 250 affordable units by 2025.
plans.source_quote: the number of housing units needed to "keep up and catch up" remains high at 960 units needed by 2026.

agencies.name: Valley Housing Fund (VHF; formerly Gunnison Valley Housing Foundation)
agencies.role: Private 501(c)(3) housing funder and convener for the whole Gunnison Valley; makes grants and low-interest loans to projects, buys and lands sites (Wilson parcel), applies for state land-banking money. Executive Director Lauren Koelliker; board president John O'Neal.
agencies.funding: Private donations and grants; founding gift from Butch and Judy Clark (proceeds of ranchland sales to the US Forest Service, 2015 and 2020); $150,000/yr Partner Support Program; $100,000 from the closing Habitat chapter (2026); $1M Prop 123 Land Banking forgivable loan (Aug 2026).
agencies.recent_activity: Aug 2026: $1M Prop 123 Land Banking award for Gunnison Rising (107 units). May 2026: sold the 3.5-acre Wilson parcel to Archway Communities for 40-75 rentals. Feb 2025: $100,000 grant to Homestead Phase 2 (Mt. Crested Butte). Over $3.1M contributed since 2010.
agencies.how_to_work_with: Apply to the Partner Support Program (six-figure awards; 75% of the $150K/yr pot goes to new construction); VHF supplied a low-interest gap loan to GardenWalk (9% LIHTC). It also partners as the nonprofit applicant on Prop 123 Land Banking (with High Mountain Concepts and NorthPoint Development at Gunnison Rising).
agencies.source_quote: VHF allocates $150,000 annually to the Partner Support Program

agencies.name: Valley Housing Fund - founding and funding model
agencies.role: Supporting source for VHF funding origin.
agencies.source_quote: The Valley Housing Fund (formerly the Gunnison Valley Housing Foundation) was founded in 2010

agencies.name: Gunnison Valley Regional Housing Authority (GVRHA) - DISSOLVED
agencies.role: Former regional housing authority (2012-2025) created by IGA among the City of Gunnison, Crested Butte, Mt. Crested Butte and Gunnison County; ran lotteries, deed-restriction compliance, rentals.
agencies.funding: Member-government contributions (about $300K/yr per 2025 HNA addendum), rental income, grants.
agencies.recent_activity: Board voted 7-2 on June 12, 2025 to recommend dissolution after five leadership changes in two years; disbanded Dec 31, 2025; duties moved to Gunnison County Housing Authority and individual towns.
agencies.how_to_work_with: Do not plan around GVRHA. Deal with the Gunnison County Housing Authority (county) and the City of Gunnison directly.
agencies.source_quote: As of December 31, 2025, the Gunnison Valley Regional Housing Authority (GVRHA) was disbanded

agencies.name: Gunnison County Housing Authority (GCHA)
agencies.role: County housing authority (est. 1979), board = Board of County Commissioners; county manager is executive secretary. Resumed active staffed operations in 2026. Builds and owns rental housing held in perpetuity; administers deed-restricted ownership programs, property management and GV-HEAT.
agencies.funding: County lodging tax (40% for housing/childcare, voter-approved 2022; about $250K/yr), linkage/impact fees ($455,999 in 2024), rent revenue from Sawtooth reinvested; county debt for Whetstone (about $130M project).
agencies.recent_activity: Owns Mountain View (30 senior/disabled units), Elk Valley (8), Sawtooth I (18) and II (32, leased 2025), Whetstone (252 units, planned 2027). Meets roughly monthly (2026 meetings listed Feb through Oct 6).
agencies.how_to_work_with: Land contributions (donated 4.5 acres for Paintbrush, land for Sawtooth, 13 acres for Whetstone), case-by-case tap fee waivers/deferrals ($15K-$25K/unit), linkage fees waived for deed-restricted rentals under 120% AMI; letters of support for state applications (approved one for VHF, Nov 4, 2025).
agencies.source_quote: Following its dissolution, the Gunnison County Housing Authority was resumed active operations with staff in 2026.

agencies.name: City of Gunnison (Community Development Dept.)
agencies.role: Land use, annexation and utilities for GEOID 0833640. Community Development Director Anton Sinkewich has been the named housing lead in public reporting; City Manager Amanda Wilson (2025). Developed Lazy K on city land; holds the $1.8M DOLA HB21-1271 grant tied to Gunnison Rising housing.
agencies.funding: No dedicated housing tax (a ballot measure failed, per the 2025 HNA addendum); housing line items in the budget ($450,000 in 2022).
agencies.recent_activity: Prop 123 opt-in Sept 26, 2023 committing 68 affordable units by end of 2026; co-adopted Gunnison Area Plan process with county (2025); took over the East Electrical Feeder project from Gunnison Rising (2025).
agencies.how_to_work_with: Per the 2025 HNA addendum: building permit and planning fees waived case-by-case (Resolution 2019-08), 50% tap fee reduction for affordable units, density bonus up to 20% for 15% affordable units, donated 4.3-acre Lazy K parcel. Constraint: city water margin is tight and the Gunnison Rising lift station is at capacity.

agencies.name: Habitat for Humanity of the Gunnison Valley - CLOSED
agencies.role: Built 19 ownership homes since 1998 (incl. Wills Way). Closed end of June 2026.
agencies.funding: Distributed remaining assets; $100,000 check to Valley Housing Fund.
agencies.recent_activity: Divested three undeveloped lots on South Eighth Street; closed June 2026.
agencies.source_quote: the local chapter of Habitat for Humanity will close at the end of June.

agencies.name: Archway Communities
agencies.role: Lakewood-based nonprofit affordable developer/owner. Bought the Wilson parcel from VHF in May 2026 for 40-75 rentals; earlier partner in the 64-unit Gunnison Rising townhome plan (2022) and the 2022 Palisades 4% LIHTC rehab attempt.
agencies.recent_activity: May 2026 acquisition of the Wilson parcel; will seek annexation and multifamily zoning.
agencies.how_to_work_with: Potential co-developer or competitor for city-area LIHTC; already holds the most LIHTC-ready rental site near the city.
agencies.source_quote: Archway Communities will work with the local government to annex and zone the land for multi-family housing.

state_funds.source_quote: The Valley Housing Fund, Gunnison - $1 million to support Gunnison Rising in Gunnison with 107 units

state_funds.program: DOLA Affordable Housing Development Incentives Grant (HB21-1271)

state_funds.source_quote: The City of Gunnison reaped $1.8 million from the program for a similar approach to supporting a planned 64-unit development of townhomes

state_funds.amount: Commitment of 68 affordable units by end of 2026 (not a grant)
state_funds.purpose: Eligibility for Prop 123 funds; missing the target loses access to Prop 123 funding in 2027
state_funds.source_quote: city council filed a commitment to create 68 affordable housing units within Gunnison's city limits over the next three years

state_funds.program: DOLA grant (via city, leveraged by VHF)
state_funds.source_quote: contributed grant funding, allowing the City to leverage an additional $1.2 million grant from CO Dept. of Local Affairs

state_funds.purpose: Concept plans for the 3.5-acre Wilson parcel
state_funds.source_quote: In 2023, VHF was awarded a Technical Assistance Grant from the Colorado Housing and Finance Authority

task_forces.name: Gunnison Valley Housing Task Force (from the One Valley Resiliency Roadmap)
task_forces.members_public: Co-led by Valley Housing Fund, Williford Consulting (Willa Williford) and GVRHA (now dissolved). Full membership not published.
task_forces.activity: Formed about 2023 for regional housing alignment; no 2025-2026 minutes, membership list or meeting schedule found.
task_forces.source_quote: The recently formed Housing Task Force, co-led by the Valley Housing Fund, Williford Consulting, and the Gunnison Valley Regional Housing Authority

task_forces.name: Gunnison County Housing Authority board (de facto regional housing body since 2026)
task_forces.activity: Public meetings roughly monthly; 2026 dates include Feb 17, Mar 3, Mar 17, Apr 14, Apr 21, May 19, Jun 16, Jul 21, Aug 4, Sep 1, Sep 15, Oct 6.
task_forces.source_quote: The Gunnison County Housing Authority's Board is made up of the members of the Board of County Commissioners

people.name: John Stock
people.public_role: Owner of High Mountain Concepts, LLC. No elected office or task-force seat found.
people.housing_involvement: Selected developer of the city-owned Lazy K parcel (MOU March 2019; 44 deed-restricted plus market homes).
people.source_quote: city leaders on Tuesday entered a memorandum of understanding with Stock for the phased development of the parcel.

people.name: John Stock
people.housing_involvement: Named partner with VHF and NorthPoint Development on the Prop 123 Land Banking application for Gunnison Rising (Nov 2025), the application funded at $1M in Aug 2026. Inference: likely the same 5-acre site, but no source states this directly.
people.source_quote: The Valley Housing Fund has thus partnered with High Mountain Concepts and NorthPoint Development to ask for a $2M forgivable loan

people.name: Lauren Koelliker
people.housing_involvement: Presented the Prop 123 Land Banking application to county commissioners, Nov 4, 2025.
people.source_quote: Valley Housing Fund Executive Director Lauren Koelliker was present for discussion.

people.name: Anton Sinkewich
people.public_role: Community Development Director, City of Gunnison
people.housing_involvement: City lead on Prop 123 opt-in and the DOLA grant; presented the Gunnison Area Plan with the county (2025).
people.source_quote: "Partnering with the county makes me much more comfortable with that commitment number."

land.source_quote: The property spans 600 acres and is a "fully-entitled, multi-phase, mixed-use development approved for more than 1,700 residential units

land.source_quote: local developer John Stock purchased five acres of land located at the western end of Gunnison Rising near the Western campus for $320,000.

land.name: Gunnison Rising - government campus lots

lihtc_and_pipeline.name: GardenWalk of Gunnison (802 N. Colorado St, city)
lihtc_and_pipeline.status: Placed in service; 9% competitive, CHFA award 2018-09-14; Belmont Development; VHF $60K low-interest loan
lihtc_and_pipeline.source_quote: GardenWalk is a Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) project that was completed in 2021.

lihtc_and_pipeline.name: Anthracite Place (Crested Butte)
lihtc_and_pipeline.source_quote: The 30-unit development is the first project in Crested Butte supported by CHFA with Low Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTC).

lihtc_and_pipeline.name: Mineral Point (Crested Butte)
lihtc_and_pipeline.source_quote: Mineral Point is a low-income housing tax credits (LIHTC) project

lihtc_and_pipeline.name: Palisades Apartments (N. Colorado St, city)
lihtc_and_pipeline.status: Not LIHTC today; Archway's 2022 4% LIHTC rehab plan did not close; a 2024 $4M private sale and GVRHA right of first refusal both withdrew. Current owner not confirmed. Preservation target.
lihtc_and_pipeline.source_quote: both the private buyers and the Gunnison Valley Regional Housing Authority withdrew as possible buyers.

lihtc_and_pipeline.name: Paintbrush Apartments (city, near Western)
lihtc_and_pipeline.status: Complete 2021; Gatesco (Gary Gates); county-donated land; 500+ waitlist at opening; not LIHTC per available sources
lihtc_and_pipeline.source_quote: Although 76 new units are entering the market, the number of potentially pre-qualified applicants on the waitlist has surpassed 500.

lihtc_and_pipeline.name: Sawtooth Phase I and II (county, near fairgrounds)
lihtc_and_pipeline.status: County-owned; Phase II leased 2025 prioritizing 80% AMI; not LIHTC
lihtc_and_pipeline.source_quote: "We prioritized 80% AMI (area median income) first, and because that is our greatest need and largest pool of applicants

lihtc_and_pipeline.name: Whetstone (county, 3 mi south of Crested Butte)

lihtc_and_pipeline.source_quote: the applicant will now set out to bring 252 rental units to the North Valley by 2027.

lihtc_and_pipeline.name: Gunnison Rising land-banking project (VHF / High Mountain Concepts / NorthPoint)
lihtc_and_pipeline.units: 107 (48 rentals at 60% AMI; 27 ownership at 100% AMI; rest market)
lihtc_and_pipeline.status: Prop 123 Land Banking $1M awarded Aug 2026; must meet statutory zoning/plan/funding milestones; a 60% AMI rental component is a natural LIHTC candidate
lihtc_and_pipeline.source_quote: 48 rental units for those earning 60% AMI plus market units.

lihtc_and_pipeline.name: Wilson parcel rentals (Archway Communities)
lihtc_and_pipeline.source_quote: The new project will provide 40-75 affordable rental homes in north Gunnison.

lihtc_and_pipeline.name: Lazy K (city)
lihtc_and_pipeline.status: Complete; 80-140% AMI; weak demand for 140% AMI units at the Dec 2022 lottery
lihtc_and_pipeline.source_quote: a total of 44 income-restricted cabins and duplexes, 3, 4 and 5-plexes will be built, along with 21 free market homes.
